correctness.rationale: Exact section normalization from coarea is 2^n f_S(0)/(n-1)!; independent Laplace Fourier inversion yields c_n P_n/D_n with c_n=2^(n-1)/(n-1)!. The numerator is polynomial by alternating Vandermonde divisibility. Pair-sum residues prove gcd(P_n,D_n)=1. Homogenization D_n-c_n z P_n is primitive and linear in z, proving absolute irreducibility by Gauss lemma. Top-degree hyperplane factors and opposite-sign parity distinguish all 2^n components. A real open graph patch in each orthant forces Zariski density. 250 exact and independent convex-hull section tests passed, but only the proof establishes the infinite-family result.

originality.rationale: General semialgebraicity and component degree bounds were established in 2021/2022; the present result sharpens them to exact degree binomial(n,2) and exactly 2^n distinct irreducible components for every n>=4. The 2024 translation paper and the 2026 restricted-section study do not state these exact all-dimensional degrees. The Fourier integral itself is known; the novel asserted part is noncancellation, irreducibility and the global degree classification. Searches found relevant but noncovering cross-polytope section face spectra and an already-known 3D specialization. Unindexed equivalents remain possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed classical exact cross-polytope section formulas or unpublished algebraic simplifications might already imply the degree statement.
Supplementary source-code collections were not exhaustively examined; the accessible project description is not whole-code evidence.

value.rationale: The all-dimensional exact degree and component count are structural invariants of a canonical geometric-tomography body, with a concrete dimension-four classification. Exact sharpness of a nontrivial published upper degree bound requires a genuine uniform noncancellation proof; the result is neither a single arbitrary finite computation nor a restatement of the known Fourier integral.
